chapter: The levee club and the St. Louis scene
title: Four-piece band at a levee club
summary: Out of school and home in Webster Groves, Thomas took a levee job in a small four-piece band with drummer Laurence Madison and altoist Tommy Starks. The cook was named Julia.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, look, what we've got to do now is we've got to get you from Jeff City to where you go from there.

Well, Jeff City, I'm still back in Webster Groves. I go back to Webster Groves to go home in summer naturally. I had And, fortunately/some things happen for me, nice things happen for me and I could take some weight off the family. See what I mean? I played the horn, you know. And, ... must be around 28 now, out of school for two years and make some money to keep things going. Going back to school. So, I got a job on the levee playing the horn and there were four of us there -- Laurence Madison.
Laurence Madison. Played drums. And, Tommy Starks whom I thought was a tremendous. Had one of the most beautiful sounds I ever heard in my life.
Alto saxophone. And the piano man I can't remember his name offhand.
Well, now when you say you were playing on the levee, what do you mean by that exactly? Where were you playing?

Well, they had spots. I'll tell you what kind of club we had. We had a spot, a very small place. We had a four piece band, a good one, too. And I think Laurence gave us a lot of advice that helped us. The piano man was of a different view. So, the spots we had were (?) was music and a little food like spaghetti. And the Negro cook's name was Julia. I'll never forget her as long as I live. Rough times, rough years. One of my last jobs going from the roadhouses (.?.) I had a guy I used to ride with on the little train called Dickie. I always thought he was musical because that's where I wrote some of my tunes.
